title: Named grid-state codes — FF_STATE
text: integer codes used LxL grids returned/accepted generate_landscape(), generate_landscape_layers() simulate_spatial_from_grid(): 1 = native vegetation (paper's \(V^{nat}\)), 2 = invader vegetation (\(V^{inv}\)), 3 = active fire (\(F\)), 4 = unoccupied, never-yet-burned space (\(\emptyset\)), 5 = unoccupied, post-fire space (\(\emptyset^F\), one two empty states long-range regrowth channel, via eta_nat/eta_inv; paper's parametrization sets eta_nat = 0, leaving invader regrowth advantage ). State 0 never appears – unused index underlying engine's state numbering.

what: Simulate the deterministic mean-field model — simulate_mean_field
title: Simulate the deterministic mean-field model — simulate_mean_field
text: Integrates mean-field ODE system describing well-mixed limit model (see paper's mean-field derivation full equations), returns full trajectory data frame. Internally uses semi-implicit (IMEX) step fire compartment stays numerically stable even paper's default L_30 = 1e6 (explicit fixed-step RK4 term alone diverges practical step size) – see package's implementation notes (vignette("forest-fire-model") NEWS.md) details. underlying vegetation/fire equations unchanged original model.

title: Simulate the spatially-explicit model from a supplied landscape — simulate_spatial_from_grid
text: Like simulate_spatial(), starts initial grid supply (typically generate_landscape_layers()) instead building one internally density2/p. Use initial condition generate_landscape() express , typically alongside rate constants zeroed isolate subset dynamics. Two useful recipes: study post-fire regrowth/colonization isolation, disable fire entirely (xi_nat = 0, xi_inv = 0, Lig_23 = 0) vegetation replacement (L_12 = 0, L_21 = 0); study fire spread isolation (e.g. starting small ignition patch -invader domain), disable colonization/regrowth (L_01 = 0, L_02 = 0, eta_inv = 0) native-side reactions (irrelevant native vegetation initial condition), keeping fire spread/burnout.
